solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Arrive early: it's what the ideal host should do

definitions.meaning: to travel quickly enough to arrive ahead of schedule

definitions.text: it's what the ideal host should do
definitions.meaning: read literally, a good host ensures guests enjoy themselves at a party

explanation.surface: A quip that a punctual guest and a generous host are the same virtue.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: a host should produce an enjoyable evening for the guests.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means progress fast on a journey, which gets you somewhere early.

clue.text: Taking in a child — a daughter by choice

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees
an option is a choice

explanation.surface: A family takes in a child, a daughter they chose for themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Legally taking a child into your family as your own is the process named.

clue.text: Stand and deliver

definitions.meaning: to stand something is to tolerate or endure it
to deliver a baby, in the mother's sense, is to give birth to it

explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes the highwayman's cry 'Stand and deliver!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerate is a synonym of one sense, and give birth (to a child) of the other.

clue.text: Military city to practise fighting with part-time soldiers

parts.note: boxers spar when they practise fighting
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A garrison town where reservists train at combat.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's reserve force of part-time volunteer soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek city-state was famous for its militaristic society and warriors.

clue.text: Embroidered mesh in mind for expensive cloth

indicators.note: the jumbled mesh letters are placed in the middle of the word for mind

parts.note: to mind something is to care for it

indicators.note: embroidering works new patterns into fabric, so the letters of mesh are reworked

explanation.surface: Fancy stitched netting is being considered as a luxurious fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Embroidered' rearranges MESH into SHME, which goes 'in' CARE.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine wool of Kashmir goats makes a famously costly textile.

clue.text: A saucepan is switched on

indicators.note: switched here means turned end to end, so the cooking vessel is read backwards

parts.note: a pot is a saucepan

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a pan on the hob has been turned on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is switched on' reads like a cooker phrase, but 'switched' is the reversal signal and 'on' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are prepositions meaning resting upon the top of something.

clue.text: Go bad, getting led astray after advert

indicators.note: the jumbled letters come after the short word for advert
led astray means led off course, so its letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is corrupted, misled by an advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' signals the anagram and 'after' puts it behind the advert abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs that rot are said to become addled, so the verb means spoil.

clue.text: Endure being in photo for modelling

indicators.note: the word for endure sits inside the short word for photo

parts.note: PIC is short for picture, a photo
to last is to endure

explanation.surface: A model must endure sitting in a photo shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for modelling' is an adjective: describing something able to be moulded.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic material can be shaped or moulded, as in the plastic arts of sculpture.

clue.text: Question: is sex confused with romance?

indicators.note: confused means muddled, so the letters of the other words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A puzzled person asks whether sex and romance are being muddled together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' mixes the letters of IS SEX and ROMANCE together.
explanation.definitionFit: To interrogate a witness in court, especially one called by the other side, is to question closely.

clue.text: Caesar's backing representative in his city

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the assembled letters are read from the end
the abbreviation for representative goes inside the name of the city

parts.note: Rome was Caesar's city

explanation.surface: Caesar is supporting a delegate in his own capital.
explanation.walkthrough: REP goes 'in' ROME to make ROREPME, and 'backing' reverses all of it. 'Caesar's' is Caesar is.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar became a title of the Roman rulers, so it stands for an imperial monarch.

clue.text: Pelvis operation reversed for large mammal

parts.note: the hip is the area around the pelvis

indicators.note: reversed means turned backwards, applied to the short form of operation

explanation.surface: A hip operation is undone to suit a big animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippopotamus, an African river animal, is among the bulkiest land beasts.

clue.text: Start to speak pompously having consumed one drink

indicators.note: consumed means swallowed, so the word for speak pompously takes the others inside it

parts.note: to orate is to speak pompously
I is the Roman numeral one
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A speaker starts holding forth after downing a single drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having consumed' puts one and the drink inside the word for speaking pompously.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to begin or arise from a source.

clue.text: Where one may find tea leaves practically secured

definitions.text: Where one may find tea leaves
definitions.meaning: loose tea is often sold in sachets, so the leaves are found within one
as good as certain, already won

explanation.surface: Tea is in its sachet and the deal is nearly done.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a result as virtually certain, like game already caught by a hunter.

clue.text: A vacant senseless fool

indicators.note: vacant means emptied, so the interior letters go and only the outer ones remain

explanation.surface: An empty-headed, witless idiot is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacant' empties SENSELESS to its outside letters, SS.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey stands proverbially for a stupid person, so the word means an idiot.

clue.text: Hazardous material? Put a distress call around first

indicators.note: the distress signal goes around the word for first

parts.note: SOS is the Morse distress signal
best is first, top-ranking

explanation.surface: Faced with dangerous stuff, one should send a mayday first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' looks like an order of action, but it is the word for top-ranking, held 'around' by the distress call.
explanation.definitionFit: The fibrous mineral is a notorious health hazard, once used in insulation.

clue.text: Hideout in which outlaw Kelly retreats

indicators.note: retreats means goes back, so the outlaw's first name is read backwards

parts.note: Ned Kelly was a famous Australian bushranger

explanation.surface: A hideaway where the bushranger Ned Kelly withdraws.
explanation.walkthrough: Ned Kelly was a 19th-century Australian outlaw; 'retreats' reverses NED.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair or secret retreat, an animal's or a gang's, is a hiding place.

clue.text: Surprising Brexit nod creates explosive situation

indicators.note: a surprising outcome is unexpected, so these letters turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: An unexpected nod to Brexit makes politics volatile.
explanation.definitionFit: A box of dry kindling ignites at a spark, so it is a metaphor for a volatile state of affairs.

clue.text: Insignificant person showing aristocrat regular letters of goodbye

parts.note: a nob is a slang term for an upper-class person

indicators.note: regular letters are every other one, taken from the farewell word

explanation.surface: A minor figure presents a nobleman with a partial farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regular letters of' GOODBYE gives its 2nd, 4th and 6th letters, ODY.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a zero who counts for nothing names a person of no importance.

clue.text: Some shenanigans turned silly

indicators.note: turned means flipped round, so the run of letters is read backwards
some of the word means only part of its letters are used

explanation.surface: Certain pranks have become foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes ENANI from inside SHENANIGANS and 'turned' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives mean senseless or lacking in substance.

clue.text: Final word is not quite correct

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the last letter of the word for correct is dropped

parts.note: to amend is to correct

explanation.surface: Someone claims a last remark isn't entirely accurate.
explanation.walkthrough: AMEND loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word said at the close of a prayer or hymn is the last word spoken.

clue.text: What's displayed by tips of stems and stalks breaking into flower?

definitions.text: What's displayed by tips of stems and stalks breaking into flower?

indicators.note: the two picked letters force their way into the word for flower

parts.note: a bloom is a flower

indicators.note: tips are the ends, here the first letters of the two plant words

explanation.surface: Asks what shows when the ends of stems and stalks open into flower.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue also describes the answer: flowers opening at the tips of a plant's shoots.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowers appearing at the tips of a plant's shoots are its bloom.

clue.text: No value keeping in shape

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the answer is held across the two words

explanation.surface: Something worthless is still kept in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' holds the answer across nO VALue; 'in shape' looks like a fitness phrase, but 'shape' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An ellipse or egg outline is a geometric figure.

clue.text: Gem dealer suspiciously pockets millions

indicators.note: pockets means takes inside, so the jumbled letters hold the abbreviation for millions
suspiciously suggests something shady, so the letters of dealer are moved around

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A shady jeweller quietly pockets a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspiciously' rearranges DEALER into EERALD, which 'pockets' M after its first E.
explanation.definitionFit: The green precious stone is a classic example of a jewel.

clue.text: Goodness found in an oak seed

indicators.note: found in means placed inside, so the exclamation goes inside the two-letter word

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like goodness

explanation.surface: Health benefits are discovered in the nut of an oak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goodness' looks like nutritional value but is the exclamation COR, British slang for 'gosh'.
explanation.definitionFit: The nut of the oak tree is its fruit, which contains the seed.
